Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

meanwhile adverb

also in the meantime, meantime, in the meanwhile, while this was going on

classical

Verg. G. 3.284: sed fugit intereā
Caes. BG 7.66.1: Intereā, dum haec geruntur

intereā

adverb · Wiktionary

meanwhile, in the meantime

The everyday word, in narrative and in talk alike; often with a dum-clause naming the other action (dum haec geruntur, while this was going on). In classical prose it always keeps its reference to time; the sense “nevertheless” grows out of it later (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • interim — meanwhile; for the moment

    adverb · also used · classical · Liv. 1.8.4: crēscēbat interim urbs; Traupman 87: meanwhile, interim · Wiktionary

    The same as intereā (Lewis & Short), and Traupman’s word for meanwhile. After Augustus it also means “for the moment, for now” and “sometimes” (Quintilian); Cicero once has it for “nevertheless” (Att. 7.12.3, Lewis & Short).

  • intereā locī — meanwhile

    phrase · also used · classical · Plaut. Men.; Ter. Eun.; Ter. Heaut. (Lewis & Short, s.v. intereā)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • sed fugit intereā, fugit irreparābile tempus

    but meanwhile time is flying, flying beyond recallVerg. G. 3.284

  • dum haec Taurus, intereā puer vēnerat et aula dēferbuerat tempusque esse coeperat edendī et tacendī

    while Taurus was saying this, the boy had come back, the pot had cooled, and it was time to eat and be quietGell. 17.8.17

  • crēscēbat interim urbs mūnītiōnibus alia atque alia appetendō loca

    meanwhile the city kept growing, taking in one place after another with its wallsLiv. 1.8.4

  • Intereā, dum haec geruntur, hostium cōpiae ex Arvernīs equitēsque quī tōtī Galliae erant imperātī conveniunt.

    Meanwhile, while this was going on, the enemy’s forces from the Arverni and the cavalry levied on the whole of Gaul gathered.Caes. BG 7.66.1

See also while, then, at once.
